chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I happen to be in the thickets, and various eggs come before me — what can I eat from them? So he (peace be upon him) said: Eat from them those whose two ends differ (i.e., the oblong ones).

key_terms.اخْتَلَفَ طَرَفَاهُ: its two ends differ — the distinguishing sign of a permissible egg; oblong shape indicating a bird of permissible species
key_terms.الْآجَام: thickets, marshes, or dense reed beds; wilderness areas away from settled habitation
key_terms.الْبَيْض: eggs (of birds); the topic of this jurisprudential ruling

ai.seo_question: Which wild eggs are halal to eat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the fiqh ruling on eating wild eggs found in dense thickets or marshes where the species is unknown. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a practical criterion: permissibility is determined by the shape of the egg — those with two different ends (oblong/asymmetrical) are permissible to eat, while those with identical ends (round/symmetrical) are not. This rule of thumb allows travelers and hunters in pre-modern Arabia to distinguish halal from haram eggs in the wild without needing to identify the bird species.
